scope: Add four explicitly authored correct-option realizations to three previously reviewed exercises. No new exercises, typed answers, prompts, targets, articles or lexical annotations. This is a presentation pilot, not expanded linguistic coverage.

historicalReview.qualification: The original source/review record describes the original single-button publication snapshot and is preserved unchanged. Its linguistic evidence is reused here; external sources were not freshly reverified for these metadata additions.

exercises.basis: The reviewed visible unmocking task and explanation explicitly accept size-relative assessment alongside のに counterexpectation.
The reviewed task accepts beginner-relative assessment without teasing or reproach; noun + のわりに contrasts with noun-predicate + なのに.

The reviewed critical task explicitly permits responsibility-relative assessment and stronger reproach, without requiring a single strongest marker. Only one added family is displayed alongside なのに per multi-correct appearance.

authorReview.notes: Checked all four labels/rationales against the complete existing prompt, visible instruction, evidence, explanation and accepted answers. Preserved the distinct framing and noun attachment rather than claiming universal synonymy.

planReview.limits: Read-only plan and pilot-context review; final rationale text and implementation were not yet present.

preservation.baselineAndroidImporter: Executed on unchanged Android 9b7cc6d with the new metadata: one test, zero skips/failures/errors.

implementationReview.scope: Final four labels/rationales against all three complete visible tasks; companion metadata diff; app implementation, new choice tests and Room schema comparison.
implementationReview.limits: Static review and narrow in-memory checks, not independent JVM/emulator execution or renewed external source verification.

authorValidation.emulator: Isolated test package on Pixel 9: naturally sampled two-correct question; both correct highlights after a wrong answer and give-up; accepted noun alternative used in the completed prompt; order preserved through vocabulary navigation and rotation.
